problems.title: Two Sum
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values in `nums`; the array is scanned once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for at most `n` entries in `seen`.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the length of `s`; each character enters and leaves the sliding window at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(min(n, a))`, where `a` is the number of distinct characters possible in the input alphabet.

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of heights; one pointer moves on every iteration.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; only two pointers and scalar values are stored.

problems.title: Longest Common Prefix
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n * (m + 1))`, where `n` is the number of strings and `m` is the shortest string length; the extra column accounts for detecting a string end, including when `m = 0`.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space, excluding the returned prefix, which uses `O(p)` space for prefix length `p`.

problems.title: 3Sum
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n²)`, where `n` is the number of values: sorting costs `O(n log n)` and the two-pointer searches cost `O(n²)`.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` worst-case auxiliary space for Python's Timsort. The returned output uses `O(r)`, where `r` is the number of triplets.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of brackets in `s`; each bracket is processed once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` in the worst case when every bracket is an opening bracket.

problems.title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(nums)`; each element after the first is inspected once and each new distinct value is written once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; distinct values are compacted in place using two indices.

problems.title: Valid Sudoku
problems.timeComplexity: `O(9 × 9) = O(1)` because the implementation inspects at most the board's fixed 81 cells.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(27 × 9) = O(1)` because the 27 row, column, and box sets each hold at most 9 digits.

problems.title: Trapping Rain Water
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of heights; the two pointers traverse the array once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; only pointers, maxima, and the accumulated result are stored.

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.timeComplexity: `O(C + 26w) = O(C + w)`, where `w` is the number of words and `C` is their total character count; each word also creates a fixed 26-count signature.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(w)` for signatures, dictionary entries, and grouped string references; the input strings themselves are not copied.

problems.title: Length of Last Word
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(s)`; splitting the string takes linear time.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` auxiliary space for the split substrings and word list.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.timeComplexity: `O(m + n)`, where `m = len(s)` and `n = len(t)`; each pointer crosses `s` at most once after `t` is counted.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(a)` for the two count dictionaries, where `a` is the number of distinct characters across `s` and `t`. The returned substring uses `O(ℓ)` for its length `ℓ`.

problems.title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of bars; every index is pushed and popped at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the monotonic stack in the worst case.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of prices; prices are scanned once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; only the minimum buy price and maximum profit are stored.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the length of `s`; each pointer moves inward at most `n` times.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; the implementation compares characters in place instead of building a normalized string.

problems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values; each unique value participates in at most one sequence scan.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the set of input values.

problems.title: Evaluate Reverse Polish Notation
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of tokens; every token is processed once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the operand stack in the worst case.

problems.title: Min Stack
problems.timeComplexity: Amortized `O(1)` per `push` or `pop` (Python list resizing); worst-case `O(1)` per `top` or `getMin`.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for `n` stored entries; each stores its value and the minimum at that depth.

problems.title: Two Sum II - Input Array Is Sorted
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values; one of the two pointers moves each iteration.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; only two pointers and the current sum are stored.

problems.title: Majority Element
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n)`, where `n = len(nums)`; each value is counted once using dictionary lookups while tracking the most frequent value.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(k)` auxiliary space for the frequency dictionary, where `k` is the number of distinct values in `nums`; `k <= n`, where `n = len(nums)`.

problems.title: Isomorphic Strings
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n)`, where `n = len(s) = len(t)` under the equal-length input constraint; sets of characters and zipped character pairs are constructed.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(min(n, a²))` auxiliary space in the worst case, where `a` is the number of distinct characters across both strings; non-isomorphic inputs can create quadratically many distinct pairs in `a`. Under the fixed ASCII alphabet constraint, this is `O(1)`.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values, to construct the set.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the set in the all-distinct case.

problems.title: Product of Array Except Self
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values; one prefix pass and one postfix pass are performed.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space when the required `O(n)` result array is excluded.

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values in `nums`; every index is added to the monotonic deque once and removed at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(k)` auxiliary space for the deque, where `k` is the window size. The returned array uses `O(n - k + 1)` space.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.timeComplexity: `O(m + n)`, where `m = len(s)` and `n = len(t)`; when the lengths match, both strings are counted in one lockstep pass.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(a)`, where `a` is the number of distinct characters across `s` and `t`.

problems.title: Encode and Decode Strings
problems.timeComplexity: Encode: `O(p²)` worst case because repeated `+=` may copy the growing immutable string. Decode: `O(p)`. Here `p` is the encoded string length, including characters, length-prefix digits, and delimiters.
problems.spaceComplexity: Encode: `O(p)` peak space for the encoded string. Decode: `O(C + w)` for the returned list and copied strings, where `C` is the decoded character count and `w` is the number of strings.

problems.title: Move Zeroes
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(nums)`; each value is inspected once and each nonzero value is swapped at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; values are rearranged in place using two indices.

problems.title: Word Pattern
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n + m)`, where `n = len(pattern)` and `m = len(s)`; splitting, hashing words, and constructing the sets take linear time in the total input size.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n + m)` auxiliary space for the split word list, copied words, and sets, where `n = len(pattern)` and `m = len(s)`.

problems.title: Reverse String
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(s)`; the two pointers swap each opposing character pair once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; characters are swapped in place using only two pointers.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values; counting, bucket creation, and bucket traversal are each linear.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the frequency map and `n + 1` buckets.

problems.title: Ransom Note
problems.timeComplexity: `O(m + n)`, where `m = len(magazine)` and `n = len(ransomNote)`; magazine characters are counted and ransom-note characters are checked once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(a)` auxiliary space for character counts, where `a` is the number of distinct characters in `magazine`; since inputs contain only lowercase English letters, `a <= 26`, so constrained space is `O(1)`.

problems.title: First Unique Character in a String
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(s)`; one pass counts characters and a second pass finds the first unique character.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space for a fixed array of 26 lowercase-English character counts.

problems.title: Is Subsequence
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(t)`; the implementation scans `t` once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)`; only the current index in `s` is stored.

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the length of `s`; each character enters once and leaves the window at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(a)` for character counts, where `a ≤ 26` for the uppercase-English input constraint, so constrained space is `O(1)`.

problems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.timeComplexity: Expected `O(n)`, where `n = len(nums)`; each value updates the prefix sum and performs a constant number of dictionary operations.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` auxiliary space for frequencies of at most `n + 1` distinct prefix sums, where `n = len(nums)`.

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.timeComplexity: `O(m + n × a)`, where `m = len(s1)`, `n = len(s2)`, and `a` is the number of dictionary keys compared per window. Since `a ≤ 26` for lowercase English letters, this reduces to `O(m + n)`.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(a)` for the `need` and `window` dictionaries; `a ≤ 26`, so constrained space is `O(1)`.

problems.title: Find Pivot Index
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(nums)`; computing the total and scanning for the leftmost pivot each take linear time.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; only the index and running sums are stored.

problems.title: Daily Temperatures
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of temperatures; every index is pushed and popped at most once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` auxiliary space for the monotonic stack; the returned array also uses `O(n)`.

problems.title: Car Fleet
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n log n)`, where `n` is the number of cars, due to sorting; the subsequent stack pass is `O(n)`.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(n)` for the sorted `(position, speed)` pairs and fleet-time stack.

problems.title: Replace Elements with Greatest Element on Right Side
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values in `arr`; the array is scanned once from right to left.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space because the input array is updated in place and returned.

problems.title: Concatenation of Array
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n` is the number of values in `nums`; each value is copied twice.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space beyond the required `O(n)` returned array.

problems.title: Append Characters to String to Make Subsequence
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(s)`; the string is scanned at most once while matching characters of `t` in order.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; only the matched-character count and target length are stored.

problems.title: Score of a String
problems.timeComplexity: `O(n)`, where `n = len(s)`; each adjacent character pair is processed once.
problems.spaceComplexity: `O(1)` auxiliary space; the generator yields one difference at a time.
